Works with

Rugged tablet for Simpro Mobile

Simpro is job management software for trade and service businesses, and its Google Play listing describes it as a complete job management software solution. The office runs Simpro Premium in a web browser for quoting, scheduling, stock and invoicing. Field staff use Simpro Mobile, an Android and iOS app that needs a mobility licence and works with Simpro Premium, to update job details, look up site and asset history, record time, present quotes, take payment and capture signatures.

Simpro Mobile is built to work away from a signal. The help guide says the first login downloads the entire set of data from Simpro Premium, which is required for the app to operate completely offline, and the FAQs say the app operates predominately offline and records a location Geostamp even with no connection. That means the device spends the day in a van, on a roof, in a plant room or under a sink, and a consumer tablet with a glass back and an unrated case is the part of the kit most likely to fail early.

This page sets out what Simpro publishes about the devices Simpro Mobile runs on, which Tuga rugged tablets and handhelds meet those published figures, where the Windows option fits, what Simpro leaves unpublished, and how a UK trade business can buy a single trial unit before ordering for the whole team.

Requirements

What Simpro Mobile needs from a device

Each item below comes from Simpro Software's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Platform: Android 8.0 or later from Google Play (the help guide quotes Android 11)

    The Google Play listing for Simpro Mobile (package com.simpro.mobile, developer Simpro Software, version 17.8.0, updated 6 October 2026) sets a minimum of Android 8.0 (API level 26) and shows device chips for Phone and Tablet. The Simpro Mobile Settings Overview in the help guide states that Simpro Mobile is available for Android 11 and iOS 16 and above. The older FAQ page still quotes Android 6 and above and lists the Samsung Galaxy S7, S8 and S9 and Google Pixel 1 and 2 as tested devices, warning that older devices may perform slowly and become unresponsive. Treat Android 11 as the safer working figure, since it is the higher of the current statements. Source: play.google.com

  • Memory, storage and screen size: not published

    Simpro does not publish a RAM, storage or screen size requirement for Simpro Mobile in the help guide pages we checked or on the Google Play listing. The help guide says loading time depends on the internet connection and your device specifications, and suggests limiting the Pre-build or Catalogue groups synced to the app and switching off the download of images and supporting materials to reduce data use and loading time. Source: helpguide.simprogroup.com

  • Offline working after a full first download

    Logging in for the first time downloads the entire set of data from Simpro Premium, which the help guide says may take some time and is required for the app to operate completely offline. After that you refresh periodically to pull updated information. The FAQs say Simpro Mobile operates predominately offline and works independently of Simpro Premium most of the time. Up to 50 drafts are kept while you stay logged in, but drafts not yet submitted to Simpro Premium are discarded if you log out, so submit quotes and jobs before logging out. The app keeps you logged in unless you tap Logout, uninstall it or clear its cache. Source: helpguide.simprogroup.com

  • Location, photos and signatures in the field

    The Google Play listing lists offline functionality, high accuracy GPS navigation, recording travel time and time on site, adding notes, photos and other attachments, and capturing staff and customer signatures with a signed job card emailed to any contact. The FAQs say that when you perform an action such as starting work, a Geostamp of your location is created even if you are offline and is submitted to Simpro Premium when you are back online. The listing also mentions taking cash or card payments in the field, with a Square Payments integration available depending on location. Source: helpguide.simprogroup.com

  • Barcode scanning: in the app for catalogue items and assets, plus a browser-based Barcoding website

    Simpro's barcoding article says that on a job in the Service Module you select +Catalogue, then the barcode icon in the search bar, and use your device to scan the item barcode. Customer assets with a barcode custom field can also be located by scan in Simpro Mobile. Barcode stocktakes and stock transfers run on a separate Simpro Premium Barcoding website (your Simpro Premium URL with /barcode added), which needs a user licence and a barcode scanner that can connect to your computer or mobile device. The article does not say whether in-app scanning uses the camera or a dedicated scan engine, and it names no supported scanner models. Source: helpguide.simprogroup.com

  • Windows: Simpro Premium in a browser, no Windows version of Simpro Mobile

    Simpro Mobile is published for Google Play and the App Store only. Simpro Premium can be used from any device or internet browser with a stable internet connection; the recommended browser is the most recent or second most recent version of Google Chrome, and Simpro says it is not optimised for other browsers although the latest versions of major browsers can be used. Logging out of Simpro Premium releases the licence for another employee. No offline mode is described for the browser version. Source: helpguide.simprogroup.com

  • NFC and RFID: not documented

    None of the Simpro pages we checked (the Simpro Mobile overview and FAQs, the barcoding article and the Google Play listing) mention reading NFC or RFID tags. Barcodes are the only identification method documented for catalogue items and assets. The NFC radio on the Tuga A10, A8 and A6 and the optional UHF RFID reader on the Tuga W10 should not be treated as Simpro features. Source: helpguide.simprogroup.com

Simpro's published Android floor is low (Android 8.0 on Google Play, Android 11 in the help guide), so the choice comes down to how a tradesperson actually uses the app: in and out of the van all day, often outdoors, offline for long stretches. The Tuga A8 runs Android 12 with Google Play, above both published figures. Its 8 inch screen gives more room than a phone for job cards, audits and presenting quote options to a customer, while still fitting one hand up a ladder or a van door pocket. The 1000 nit screen stays readable in direct sun, the 8000mAh battery is removable so a charged spare can take over on a long day, and VESA mount points with a pogo pin connector let it lock into the vehicle mounting dock between jobs. Simpro publishes no RAM figure; the A8 has 6GB and 128GB of storage for the full offline data download. The trade-offs against the A10 are real: the A8 is sealed to IP67 rather than IP68, has no MIL-STD rating and a 1280 x 800 screen. At £379 it is £70 less than the A10.

Worth knowing. Simpro Mobile has no Windows version, so the Tuga W10 can only run Simpro Premium and the Barcoding website in a browser, with a stable internet connection and no documented offline mode; it is a stores, workshop or cabin device, not an engineer's field device. Simpro's published Android figures disagree (Android 8.0 on Google Play, Android 11 in the settings overview, Android 6 on an older FAQ page), and it publishes no RAM, storage or screen size requirement, so trial one unit with your own Simpro build and data before ordering for a team. Simpro does not say whether in-app barcode scanning uses the camera or a scan engine and names no supported scanners, so the A6's Zebra 2D scan engine and the W10's optional scanner are not documented Simpro inputs. NFC and RFID are not documented by Simpro, so the NFC on the A10, A8 and A6 and the optional UHF RFID reader on the W10 should not be counted as Simpro features. Simpro Mobile needs a mobility licence assigned in Simpro Premium.
Setting up

Getting Simpro Mobile running

  1. Ask your Simpro administrator to assign the engineer a mobility licence and the right security group permissions in Simpro Premium. Without a mobility licence you cannot log in to Simpro Mobile.
  2. On the Tuga A8, A10 or A6, open Google Play and install Simpro Mobile (package com.simpro.mobile, developer Simpro Software).
  3. On first launch, enter your workspace (the part of your Simpro Premium web address after https:// and before .simpro) and check the domain shown below it, then log in with your Simpro Premium username and password or single sign-on if your company has set it up.
  4. Stay on a good Wi-Fi or 4G connection while the first login downloads the full data set; this is what lets the app work offline. To shorten it, limit the Pre-build and Catalogue groups under System > Setup > Mobile > Simpro Mobile, and consider switching off the download of images and supporting materials in the app's Settings.
  5. Submit quotes and jobs back to Simpro Premium before you log out, because unsubmitted drafts are discarded at logout. Refresh periodically when you have signal to pull schedule changes.
  6. If you use barcodes, test scanning a catalogue item from +Catalogue on a Service Module job, and test the Barcoding website at your Simpro Premium URL with /barcode added, before rolling out.
  7. Fit the vehicle mounting dock for the A8 or A10 in the van, the charging dock for an A10 or W10 that lives in the office, or the belt holster for the A6. Fit the tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out.
